solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Squads back in uniform before training session initially

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: back says the little word in is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of training and of session

explanation.surface: A sports report: the squads are back in team kit before the opening training session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IN into NI; 'initially' takes T and S from training session.
explanation.definitionFit: Units and squads are both small organised groups, of soldiers or players, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Ambition in combination with skill is OK

indicators.note: in says the ambition sits inside the combination

parts.note: a union is a combination of parts
an object is a goal or ambition
able means skilful, with skill

explanation.surface: Ambition combined with skill is perfectly acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination' reads like a skill set; here it is a union, as of workers. 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody would object to is acceptable, all right.

clue.text: Run into S American once leaving a historic city

indicators.note: leaving says the letter a departs from the word

parts.note: an Inca was one of the people of Peru before the Spanish conquest
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An Inca leaves an ancient city in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes A from INCA.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a debt or penalty is to run into it.

clue.text: Having dashed inside, one's brought up teaching schedules

indicators.note: brought up in a down entry means the whole is read upwards
having it inside says one piece holds the other
inside says the dashed word goes within the one's

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S
bally is an old British euphemism for 'damned', as dashed is

explanation.surface: Someone dashes inside and finds their teaching timetable has been raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dashed' is not running: like 'bally', it is a mild British oath. 'Having ... inside' signals the insertion and 'brought up' reads the whole upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabuses are the plans of what a course teaches, teaching schedules.

clue.text: In play, Charlie gets oddly sluggish

indicators.note: in play means set loose and moving about, so the letters are rearranged
oddly takes the first and third letters of gets, the odd-numbered ones

explanation.surface: A sports scene: when the ball is live, a player called Charlie turns oddly slow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' gives GT from gets; 'In play' shuffles CHARLIE with GT. Charlie is taken whole here, not as C.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic describes someone drowsy and lacking energy, which is what sluggish means.

clue.text: Joint leaders of industry non-committal at first

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Industry chiefs give a joint statement that commits them to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective with 'leaders'; it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A loin is a cut of meat, which a butcher calls a joint.

clue.text: I'm stealing misplaced report of the enemy's progress?

indicators.note: misplaced says the letters are put in the wrong places, rearranged

explanation.surface: A spy admits stealing a misplaced dispatch about enemy movements.
explanation.walkthrough: Time is the enemy, as in Yeats's 'no enemy but time'; the pips report its progress.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcast pips mark the passing hours, reporting how far time has advanced.

clue.text: Outdated transporter freshens fruit

parts.note: airs means freshens, as a room or laundry
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: An old delivery van that airs out its fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppelins and similar dirigibles were early aircraft, now an obsolete means of carrying passengers.

clue.text: A large nut supply to grind

indicators.note: supply read as supple-y, in a supple way, says the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: A big supply of nuts ready to be milled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun; read it as the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: To granulate is to reduce to grains, crushing as a mill does.

clue.text: Gasp in surprise: I disturbed bathers

parts.note: to catch someone is to surprise them
I am one person, so I is one

indicators.note: disturbed says these letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: Swimmers gasp in surprise when someone disturbs their bathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges BATHERS to SBREATH.
explanation.definitionFit: To gasp is to draw a sudden sharp breath, as one does pausing to recover.

clue.text: Arcane pursuit last month featured in violent comics

indicators.note: featured in says one piece appears inside the other
violent suggests the letters of comics are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old business letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that last month's violent comic books dabbled in something arcane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last month' is the old commercial abbreviation ult. (ultimo). 'violent' signals the anagram and 'featured in' the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Occultism is the study of hidden, secret, supernatural matters, an arcane pursuit indeed.

clue.text: Cook's pan

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in an oven
to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does

explanation.surface: A cook's pan, as if naming a kitchen utensil.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both baking meat in the oven and savaging a performance in a review.

clue.text: Golden days during month in the country

indicators.note: during says these pieces fall within the month

parts.note: Jan is short for January
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Golden days spent abroad for a month somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold is 'or' in heraldry. 'during' signals the insertion into the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Jordan is a Middle Eastern kingdom, so it is a country.

clue.text: Like a small bully boy casing hotel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: casing says the bully boy wraps round the hotel letter

parts.note: a tough is a rough, bullying man
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A little thug sizing up a hotel before a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully boy' looks like THUG, which has no O; the word is TOUGH. 'casing' puts H inside TOUGH after the OUG.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Like' as in 'it looks like rain' means as if, the same as the conjunction in the grid.

clue.text: Make fast roller a time-saver at Wimbledon

parts.note: to tie is to make fast, secure
a breaker is a big wave, a roller

explanation.surface: Getting a fast serve to save time in a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the London tennis championship; a long set is cut short by a deciding game.
explanation.definitionFit: This deciding game ends a set at six all, shortening matches rather than playing on.

clue.text: Upsetting measurement system outfitter's familiar with?

definitions.meaning: a hatter or outfitter knows how hats are sized, read as two words

explanation.surface: A grumble that an outfitter's measuring system is upsetting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat being turned upside down is overturning, which is what upsetting means of a vessel.

clue.text: Barred musical movement involving about 500

indicators.note: involving says the movement takes in the about letter

parts.note: a prelude is an introductory piece of music
c. for circa means about
D is 500 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A musical movement involving some 500 bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' leans on music's bars; here it means prevented. C goes after PRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to rule it out, prevent it, so barred.

clue.text: Patent scheme I introduced

indicators.note: introduced says I is brought into the scheme word

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: An inventor files a patent for a scheme of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patent' looks like an inventor's noun; here it is the adjective meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or clear, as in plain to see.

clue.text: The setter had brief simple clues

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so 'I had' is I'D

indicators.note: brief says the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: easy means simple

explanation.surface: The setter admits to having written brief, easy clues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops Y from EASY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas are hints or notions, as in 'I have no clue' meaning no idea.

clue.text: Timber to support Spartan characters climbing shaft

indicators.note: to support says the timber goes below in a down answer
climbing in a down entry means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter, so Greek letters are nus
a beam is a piece of timber

explanation.surface: A timber beam propping up Greek lettering on a mine shaft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses NUS to SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light is a single ray, as a beam from the sky is.

clue.text: Dozy supporter more often away

parts.note: a bra supports, a crossword favourite
away more often means at home less, so 'in less'

explanation.surface: A sleepy fan who travels to away games more often than not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more often away' turns round to 'in less': if you are away more, you are in less.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozy in British slang means stupid, as brainless does.

clue.text: Why craftsmen can't grip religious recruits?

definitions.meaning: a workbench lacking clamps cannot hold work, read as two words
newcomers to a religious order, not yet professed

explanation.surface: A joking question about clumsy craftsmen and new religious recruits.
explanation.walkthrough: The vices are bench clamps, not sins, which also suits recruits to holy orders.
explanation.definitionFit: These are beginners in a religious order, on probation before taking vows.

clue.text: Revolutionary working extended? Not any more

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is
longer means extended

explanation.surface: A revolutionary who once worked extended hours does so no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns ON into NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means no more, having stopped, which is not any more.

clue.text: Artful Dodger always got round Bill

indicators.note: got round says the word for always encircles the bill

parts.note: ever means always
an ad is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: Dickens's Artful Dodger always got round Bill Sikes.
explanation.walkthrough: In Oliver Twist the Artful Dodger and Bill Sikes are in the same gang; here Dodger is just one who dodges.
explanation.definitionFit: An artful dodger is a cunning escaper, one who slips out of things.

clue.text: New York chum served up excellent port

indicators.note: served up in a down entry means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: bud is American slang for friend
A1 means excellent, written with I for the 1

explanation.surface: A New York pal serves up some excellent port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: This Gulf emirate's city has major seaports, so it is a port.

clue.text: Cross but not completely thank heavens!

indicators.note: but not completely says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An exclamation of relief at not being quite angry.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Egyptian looped cross, a symbol of life.

clue.text: Yield from funds reduced

indicators.note: reduced says the word is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: a budget is a sum of funds

explanation.surface: Lower returns from investment funds after cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yield' looks like financial return; here it is giving way.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give way or move, as in refusing to budge.

clue.text: Hooded Asian ruler leading troops on horse

indicators.note: leading says the ruler comes first
on says the troops come after the horse in an across entry

parts.note: a king is a ruler
a cob is a sturdy horse
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: An Asian monarch in a cloak leads his troops into battle on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooded Asian' is a snake, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake of South and South-East Asia spreads a hood behind its head.

clue.text: No-hoper confused with MD, a stout fellow

indicators.note: confused says these letters are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written; doctor of medicine

explanation.surface: A hopeless case gets mixed up with a doctor, a sturdy chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout fellow' sounds like a decent chap; it means a heavily built one.
explanation.definitionFit: This body type is the rounded, heavily built one, so a fat person is one.

clue.text: Strike abruptly terminated by hospital worker

indicators.note: abruptly terminated says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to smite is to strike
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital worker's strike is suddenly called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly terminated' drops E from SMITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith or metal craftsman is a worker at the forge.
